stemBlocks.value: The matrices A and B satisfy A + B = C, where A = (2 −3 / 1 4) and C = (7 1 / −2 9). (a) Determine the matrix B. (b) Verify that B + A = C.
Think first: Rearranging A + B = C gives B = C − A, exactly as you would with ordinary numbers.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p197-q07 from workbook page 197.

solutionSteps.instruction: Rearrange the equation to make B the subject.

contentBlocks.value: A + B = C, so B = C − A.

solutionSteps.instruction: Subtract each entry of A from the matching entry of C.
Add A to B and compare with C.

strategyBlocks.value: Make B the subject by subtracting A from C, then add A back to the answer to confirm it returns C.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) B = C − A = (5 4 / −3 5)  (b) B + A = (5 + 2, 4 + (−3) / −3 + 1, 5 + 4) = (7 1 / −2 9), which is exactly C, so the answer checks out.

whyThisWorks.value: Matrix addition is done entry by entry, so a matrix equation can be rearranged in the same way as a numerical one. Matrix addition is also commutative, which is why B + A gives the same result as A + B and makes the verification valid. The check catches sign errors, particularly at 1 − (−3).

commonErrors.misconception: Computing A − C instead of C − A.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Computing A − C instead of C − A.
